newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - UK PENSIONS.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - UK PENSIONS.

text.p: "Inefficient", "expensive selling methods", "unnecessarily complex" marketing are not words any industry wants to see used to describe it. Yet these were just some of the phrases in today's Office of Fair Trading report on Britain's pension providers.

Many have criticised the industry since the scale of mis-selling began to emerge four years ago. In the last few months, the new Government has singled out pension providers -- primarily insurers and banks -- by naming and shaming those who have dragged their feet over compensation.
The OFT has gone a step further by coming up with its own blue-print for a simple, cheap system of personal pensions for all. If adopted, it could spell bad news for pension providers.

The OFT scheme would slash the opportunities for fund management fees by using passively managed tracker funds. Distribution charges would also come under tighter scrutiny, as would the practice of loading charges at the beginning of a contract.

A recent newsletter from actuaries and consultants Bacon & Woodrow took up a similar theme, arguing that many pension providers face a serious commercial and financial problem. Consumers are becoming better informed about pensions and new suppliers are beginning to challenge the practices of the traditional pension providers.
The article concludes that many life insurance marketing people say marketing is about satisfying chosen customer needs, forgetting that this must be done at an acceptable level of profit.

The new government has said it will review the provision of pensions for all. Many life insurers believe that this will lead to opportunities for them. However, there are scenarios which could involve very slim pickings indeed.
